Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 43, verse 1:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Zukhruf (Ornaments/Adornment), because the word zukhruf, meaning gold, is mentioned in it in the context of describing some of the fleeting pleasures of this world, and comparing them with the lasting bounties of the Hereafter.

From the objectives of the surah

• To demonstrate that the polytheists acknowledged Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (the Oneness of Lordship), which necessarily entails Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (the Oneness of Divinity), and to express wonder at their condition: they confess that Allah is their Creator and the Creator of all creatures, yet nevertheless they have taken partners who are powerless to benefit, to harm, or to exercise any control.

• To refute the beliefs of the polytheists concerning the angels, for they made them daughters of Allah and worshipped them, while they themselves held that daughters are of lesser worth than males, and their basis for this was the imitation of their forefathers; and to refute their claim that they follow the millah (religion) of Ibrahim (Abraham).

• To show that worldly wealth is not a measure of Allah's love for a servant. The polytheists found it unlikely that the message would be sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), who was an orphan and poor, and they desired that revelation be sent to a great man possessed of standing and wealth. The Qur'an rejected these earthly, false values.

• To present the story of Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus), peace be upon them, in their calling of their peoples to Tawhid, and how the peoples divided into factions and how their end turned out; as consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding what the objectors among the chiefs of his people raised against his being chosen for the message, their pride in false values and the goods of worldly life, and their contempt for him.

• The warning of the Hour coming suddenly, the depiction of the state of people in the scene of the Resurrection, the description of the condition of the believers after their entry into Paradise, followed by the condition of the criminals in Hell, and a reminder to them that the angels record their deeds, and that the punishment they are in is caused by their deeds.

[Tafsir]

Indeed, the descent of ʿIsā (peace be upon him) before the Day of Resurrection is a proof that the Hour is near. So do not doubt that it will certainly come to pass. And follow me in what I inform you of from Allah, the Exalted; this is a straight path to Paradise, with no crookedness in it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 43, verse 62:

What I have commanded you, namely taqwa (God-consciousness) of Allah and devoting worship exclusively to Him in His divinity (uluhiyyah), is the straight path, and it is the true religion of Allah, which He does not accept from anyone other than it.

The Christian sects differed concerning the matter of Isa (peace be upon him), and they became factions regarding him. Among them are those who acknowledge that he is the servant of Allah and His messenger, and this is the truth. Among them are those who claim that he is the son of Allah, and among them are those who say that he is Allah. Allah is exalted far above what they say, an exceedingly great exaltation. So there is destruction and a painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection for those who described Isa with other than what Allah described him with.

So leave them, O Messenger, to plunge into their falsehood and amuse themselves with their worldly life, until they meet their Day, the Day they are promised (with punishment): whether in this world, or in the Hereafter, or in both together.

And He is Allah alone, the one truly worthy of worship in the heavens and on the earth. He is the All-Wise, who perfected His creation and made His law flawless, the All-Knowing of everything concerning the affairs of His creatures; nothing about them is hidden from Him.

Blessed be Allah, and abundant is His goodness, and great is His dominion, the One to whom alone belongs the sovereignty of the seven heavens and the seven earths and whatever is between them, all things. With Him is the knowledge of the Hour, the time when the Resurrection will take place, when creation will be gathered from their graves to the place of reckoning. And to Him you will be returned, O people, after your death, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 43, verse 86:

Those whom the polytheists worship do not possess intercession with Him for anyone, except those who bear witness to the truth, affirming the Oneness of God and the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they know the reality of what they affirmed and testified to.

And if you were to ask them, O Messenger, those polytheists among your people, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah created us." So how are they turned away and diverted from the worship of Allah, and how do they associate others with Him?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 43, verses 88–89:

Muhammad (ﷺ) said, complaining to his Lord about his people who denied him: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe in You or in what You sent me to them with." So Allah commanded him to turn away from them and from their harm, and to leave them because of their disbelief and obstinacy. Nothing should come from you, O Messenger, except the greeting of peace to them, which is what people of intellect and insight say to the ignorant. They do not revile them or treat them with the like of their evil deeds. "They will soon know" what trials and punishment they will meet. In this there is a severe threat and warning to these obstinate disbelievers and those like them.
